The 40th plenary meeting of the General Assembly is called to order. The Assembly will resume its consideration of agenda item 89, entitled "Report of the International Atomic Energy Agency", to continue the debate on the item. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of El Salvador.

Thank you, President. Allow me to begin by expressing the thanks of El Salvador for the convening of this plenary debate on the annual report of the International Atomic Energy Agency. My country is proud to participate in this forum, which reflects our steadfast commitment to the founding principles of the agency, atoms for peace, development, and international cooperation. El Salvador reiterates It's recognition of the work of the IAEA under the leadership of the Director General, Rafael Mariano Grossi, particularly in nuclear security, radiological protection, peaceful uses of nuclear science, combating cancer, food security and human capacity building. El Salvador believes that the implementation of a nuclear energy program stands as a strategic tool to allow us to reach our national development goals. Nuclear energy represents an alternative to guarantee a reliable, accessible, and environmentally friendly energy supply for future generations. With this in mind, in 2024, the legislature adopted, with a broad consensus, the atomic energy law, making us the first Central American country to adopt a comprehensive legal framework in this area. This law regulates all activities throughout the lifecycle of nuclear fuel and guarantees the highest standards of safety, radiological protection, transparency, and exclusively peaceful use. To implement this vision, the government established an agency to implement the nuclear energy program in El Salvador. This is under the Radio Lemper Commission. It is responsible for strategic planning, carrying out feasibility studies for a nuclear electric plant, and training human talent. In accordance with the international legal framework, in 2024, El Salvador ratified and deposited at the IAEA the following key instruments: the Convention on Nuclear Security, the Vienna Convention on Civil Liability for Damage, and the Safeguards and Immunities Agreement. Further, as part of the commitments under the Convention on Nuclear Security, El Salvador presented its first national report. This sets out our legal framework, security measures, and institutional mechanisms to allow us to guarantee the future functioning of nuclear facilities in a safe and responsible manner. We are currently implementing our national programmatic framework for 2024 to 2029. Under this, we have adopted 4 projects. for a cooperation framework with the IAEA for the biennium 2026 to 2027. This covers areas such as health, energy, environment and water management. To date, almost 200 Salvadoran professionals have been trained by the IAEA through regional workshops, regional and interregional projects. in areas such as nuclear law, radiological safety, nuclear medicine, cancer, agriculture, food security, managing water resources and the environment, as well as strategic planning and energy. El Salvador would like to thank the IAEA for its trust in the country to allow it to be the headquarters of activities such as a regional course on establishing a national position for a new nuclear energy program that was held in July this year. This allowed us to train national and regional level professionals. And in November 2025 in San Salvador, we will host a regional meeting on energy planning following the methodology climate, land and water. This falls under the ACO framework. We would like to take this opportunity to express our readiness to host similar activities in the future. On the margins of the 69th General Conference of the IEA, we reaffirmed the Regional Framework Agreement. Since 2021, we have been actively involved in this regional mechanism. In 2024, our country received a financial contribution under AECAL, which we have used to strengthen scientific databases, provide technical materials, and to organize regional events and ensure the participation of national experts. We reaffirm our commitment to the IAEA's technical fund. For 2025, we made a voluntary contribution, and we have pledged to also contribute in 2026. My country maintains an aspiration to join the Board of Governors of the IAEA for 2024 to 2028. We are convinced that we can provide a perspective from developing countries that have opted for the peaceful, safe and responsible use of nuclear energy. El Salvador would like to conclude this statement by paying tribute posthumous tribute to Ambassador Julia Vallatoro Talio, who was the permanent representative of El Salvador to international bodies headquartered in Vienna, who chaired the Group of Friends of Women in Nuclear Energy. headquartered in Vienna. Her leadership underscores the relevance of the full, effective and meaningful participation of women in the nuclear sphere and reaffirmed El Salvador's commitment to the equality and inclusion of women in science and nuclear technology. Thank you very much.
I thank the distinguished representative of El Salvador. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Kazakhstan.

Mr. President, distinguished delegates, at the outset, allow me to express our sincere appreciation to Director General Rafael Grossi for his comprehensive and insightful report. We commend his tireless efforts in advancing the mission of the International Atomic Energy Agency in the fields of peaceful uses of nuclear energy, nuclear safety, and nonproliferation. The Kyrgyz Republic fully supports the goals and principles enshrined in the IAEA Statute. We highly value the Agency's vital role in strengthening the nuclear and radiation safety, providing technical assistance and fostering international cooperation in the peaceful application of atomic energy. In recent years, the Kyrgyz Republic, in close partnership with international organizations and financial institutions, has achieved the tangible progress in addressing issue of radiation and environmental safety. Environmental protection and sustainable development remain among our top national and global priorities. Kyrgyzstan continues to actively cooperate with the IAEA through its technical cooperation programs in medicine, agriculture, environmental protection and human resource development. We attach particular importance to the use of nuclear and isotopic technologies in the diagnosis and treatment of cancer, which directly contributes to improving the quality of health care in our country. We firmly believe that the peaceful atom must serve the people, bringing practical benefits and support the achievements of the SDGs. Kyrgyzstan is interested in expanding such cooperation, especially in the context of sustainable development and climate change adaptation. To strengthen the legal framework of nuclear and radiation safety and in line with the international instruments and AIA standards, The Kyrgyz Republic continues to improve its national legislation. We have ratified the Convention on Assistance in the Case of the Nuclear Accident or Radiation Emergency, the Convention on Early Notification Nuclear Accident, and the Additional Protocol to the Safeguard Agreements with the IAEA under the TPNW. In October this year, Kyrgyzstan and IAEA signed a new country program framework for 2026 and 2031. The key document defines our national priorities for technical cooperation in the coming years. The Kyrgyz Republic remains firmly committed to the nonproliferation regime, supports the efforts to strengthen the IAEA safeguards system, and calls upon all states to strictly fulfill its international obligation in this vital area. In conclusion, Mr. President, Kyrgyzstan reaffirms its readiness to continue active engagement with the Agency to deepen cooperation and the shared experience in order to promote the safe, secure, and peaceful use of nuclear energy.

Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Kyrgyzstan. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Kazakhstan.

Distinguished Chair, Excellencies, let me begin by expressing my sincere gratitude to the permanent missions of Australia in Vienna and New York for their leadership in facilitating the resolution entitled Report of the International Atomic Energy Agency. Alexander reaffirms its strong support for the IAEA's indispensable role in promoting the peaceful uses of atomic energy, strengthening nuclear safety, verification, and security. However, despite the agency's impeccable record, I must raise concern about an absolutely unacceptable and flawed practice within the organization. The principle of sovereign equality of all member states clearly articulated in its statute, remains not yet fully realized. The IAEA continues to operate under a structural imbalance that prevents some Member States, including Kazakhstan, from assuming their rightful place in its decision-making processes. Kazakhstan has consistently and resolutely raised this issue to restore fairness, inclusiveness and justice within the Agency. The present resolution reflects this principled position and draws attention to the developments highlighted during the 69th session of the IAEA General Conference. Excellencies, I would like to draw your attention to the footnotes of the resolution, which recall the IAEA General Conference resolution entitled "Restoration of the sovereign equality of Member States in the IAEA". adopted in September 2023 at Kazakhstan's initiative. It seeks to ensure equal rights and representation for 13 so-called "airless" states, those not yet included in any regional group defined by Article 4.A of the Statute. Being airless means being a full-fledged member of the IAEA yet deprived of the right to be elected to the Board of Governors, to hold leadership positions, or to join regional consultations that shape key decisions. Can you imagine that a full-fledged member cannot join the so-called informal regional group, when here in New York, all member states are admitted to regional groups automatically? Such a situation is neither fair nor consistent with the Statute. Kazakhstan firmly rejects this inequality, which also affects other Central Asian states committed to the Agency's principles and objectives. Distinguished delegates, Kazakhstan's record in advancing the peaceful use of nuclear energy is beyond the question. We voluntarily renounced the world's fourth largest nuclear arsenal, closed the Semipalatinsk test site, commemorated globally as the International Day Against Nuclear Tests; together with the Central Asian neighbors, established the Central Asian Nuclear-Weapon-Free Zone; hosts the IAEA Low Enriched Uranium Bank; remains the world's leading producer and exporter of natural uranium. Throughout its membership, Kazakhstan has always paid its assessed contributions fully and on time. and has regularly provided voluntary contributions to IAEA programmes, a clear demonstration of our enduring commitment to the Agency's mandate and collective responsibility. Nevertheless, for more than three decades, imagine, three decades, Kazakhstan and its neighbors have faced unjustified barriers to full participation in the Agency's governance. Your Excellencies, at the recent 69th session of the IAEA General Conference, Kazakhstan announced its candidacy for the Board of Governors for the 25-27 term from the Far East area, consistent with its membership in the UN Asia-Pacific Group. While some viewed this as a challenge to informal regional arrangements, Most recognized it as a legitimate exercise of our sovereign right. Following broad consultations, Kazakhstan yet again demonstrated flexibility and withdrew its candidacy as our application for membership in the Far East Regional Group was placed on the silence procedure until the next session of the IAEA Board of Governors in November this year. Kazakhstan has been seeking this membership since 2009, and enjoys the support of all members of the group, yet our application has been repeatedly delayed by one state. We sincerely hope that this time the silence procedure will pass successfully. If not, Kazakhstan will continue to assert and defend its legitimate rights in full accordance with the statute of the organization, and speaking publicly out about those who prevent the progress in this overdue issue. Distinguished delegates, in conclusion, Kazakhstan always acts responsibly and constructively within the IAEA and among its member states. Our case is not the only one. As I have mentioned already, there are 13 AELIS states in the IAEA. Our case is not about politics. It is about upholding the Agency's core values. sovereign equality, fair representation, and democratic justice. If these principles are compromised, the credibility and sustainability of the Agency itself is at risk. Through dialogue, mutual respect, and shared commitment to equality, we can strengthen the unity and effectiveness of the Agency for the benefit of all of us. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Kazakhstan. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea.

Mr. President, The delegation of DPRK expressed its grave concern over the draft resolution, report of the IAEA, submitted to this meeting, containing so-called resolution of the IAEA General Conference that unreasonably took issue with the DPRK's exercise of its sovereign right. In this regard, I clarify our position. The DPRK is steadily building up its strength in the face of ever-worsening security environment on the Korean Peninsula and in its vicinity. due to expansion of the US-led nuclear bloc. This is indisputable, independent right of the sovereign state. DPRK's transition to nuclear weapon state was inevitable choice made at the crossroad of rise and fall of our state. And now, the concept of the denuclearization have already lost its meaning. As a physical cornerstone for safeguarding national security and peace and stability of the region and the rest of the world, DPRK's position of the nuclear weapon has been permanently enshrined in the national law. And it is our obligation to defend national law without fail. Moreover, the DPRK withdrew from the IAEA more than 30 years ago. and stands as a nuclear-weapon state outside NPT. Therefore, the IAEA has neither a legal authority nor moral justification whatsoever to interfere in our internal affairs. However, the IAEA put on its agenda the legitimate exercise of the right to self-defense of the sovereign states outside its jurisdiction. This constitutes intolerable political provocation and clear interference in our domestic affairs. The DPRK condemns and rejects such acts in the strongest terms. Unless the nuclear threat from outside is terminated, and as long as there exist imperialist forces that rely on the nuke for the means of existence of their tyranny, We will never allow the interruption on our road of bolstering up our nuclear deterrence. Mr. President, at the General Conference of the IAEA held last September, the responsible nuclear weapons states and several IAEA member states expressed resolute and head-on opposition and rejection to the adoption of the illegal anti-DPRK resolution. That is vivid reflection of the international desire to put an end to decades-old practice of injustice and to defend justice and equity. Comrade Kim Jong-un, President of State Affairs of DPRK, said, "The fact that DPRK is possessed of nuclear weapon will remain forever as it is now, regardless of whether United States and its allies like it or not. And no matter how loudly or persistently they call the colors for denuclearization for 10, 20, 50, or even 100 years, history will not be rewritten, nor will the reality will be changed, even though United States and its allies continue to possibly adopt such unfeasible documents under the name of the so-called international organization, and the attempt to deny DPRK's status as a nuclear weapon state. We clarify once again that DPRK will have nothing to do with the IAEA, which is devoid of the intrinsic principle of independence, impartiality, and objectivity in its activity, and instead continue to pursue biased and double-dealing practice by aligning itself with the United States and its hostile policy against DPRK. The delegation of DPRK take this opportunity to recommend that IAEA should focus its undivided attention on addressing the real and urgent threat undermining the foundation of the international nuclear nonproliferation regime, such as provision of the extended deterrence, nuclear sharing with non-nuclear weapon states, and transfer of the nuclear submarine technology conducted by the United States, rather than wasting time and resources on the issue beyond its mandate. DPRK will in the future, too, categorically oppose and reject any attempt to modify current status of DPRK and fulfill its obligation before the international community as a responsible nuclear weapon state. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Togo.

Thank you, Mr. President. The delegation of Togo welcomes the presentation of the 2024 report of the International Atomic Energy Agency, and we're grateful for the additional information provided on its activities. We'd like to congratulate the Director General, Mr. Rafael Mariano Grossi, and his whole team for the remarkable results that they've seen in implementing the agency's mandate. Togo reaffirms its full support for the IEA's work, which remains an essential partner in preventing nuclear proliferation and promoting the inalienable right to the peaceful use of nuclear energy. Through its technical and scientific support, the Agency makes a tangible contribution to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals. My delegation is pleased to note that the 2024 report highlights the significant progress made in innovative programmes such as Rays of Hope, This promotes access to cancer treatment. Another program is ZODIAC in the detection of zoonotic diseases. We have New Tech Plastics against plastic pollution and finally Atoms for Food for food security and nutrition. For its part, Togo joined seven other member states in the 24th Safeguards Traineeship Programme for Young Professionals held in Vienna from February to October 2024. This contributes to strengthening to human capacity building in nuclear safeguards. President, since joining the IAEA in 2012, Togo has maintained dynamic cooperation with the Agency, bolstered by our signing of the Country Programme Framework for 2020-2025. This covers five priority areas. They are nuclear and radiological safety, health and nutrition, food and agriculture, water and the environment, and energy and mines. Through this partnership, Togo has received major technical support, particularly for the establishment of an international oncology center in Lome, which has been functioning since 2022, contributing to improving access to cancer care in the subregion. In the same vein, the Applied Hydrology and Environmental Geology Lab at Lome University received an isotopic analyzer provided by the IAEA. This has improved water resource management. During the COVID-19 pandemic, Togo also received material and technical support from the IAEA, particularly through the provision of RT-PCR machines, diagnostic kits, and training, which boosted our health system's resilience. President, COGHO welcomes the excellent cooperation that we have with the IAEA. This bears out its constant commitment to the three pillars of the non-proliferation treaty. They are disarmament, non-proliferation, and the peaceful use of nuclear energy for peaceful means. In a world marked by persistent tensions and manifold crises, nuclear energy must be seen as a tool for hope and progress. for sustainable development, particularly for developing countries facing the challenges of poverty, food security, and access to water and health. My delegation therefore calls for enhanced international cooperation with the IAEA so as to boost the impact of its programs and guarantee that the benefits of nuclear science reach us all. In parallel, Togo underscores that the peaceful use of atoms must go hand in hand with heightened efforts to ensure the full elimination of nuclear weapons, whose mere existence remains a threat to collective security, 80 years after the tragedies of Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Finally, as a newly elected member of the IAEA Council of Governors, Togo reiterates its commitment to work to consolidate the Agency's mandate and to promote atoms for peace, development and well-being. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Togo. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Kenya.

Thank you, Mr. President. Kenya welcomes the annual report of the International Atomic Energy Agency for 2024 and commends the Director General for his leadership in advancing the agency's mandate as set out in its statute and takes note of the draft resolution before this Assembly, which underscores the indispensable role of the agency in fostering international peace and security through these barriers. We recognize the International Atomic Energy Agency as a vital bearer of the global security architecture, whose role has grown in urgency and relevance amid today's geopolitical turmoil. My delegation commends the Agency's efforts to strengthen international framework for nuclear safety and security, enabling member states, especially developing countries, to harness nuclear science for national development and contribute to achieving the sustainable development goals. Kenya commends the Agency's strengthened engagement with Africa, including through the African Regional Cooperative Agreement for Research, Development and Training Related to Nuclear Science and Technology, and cooperation with the African Commission on Nuclear Energy under the Berendaba Treaty. Mr. President, in the area of human health, Kenya takes positive note of the Agency's continued support to Member States in strengthening their national capacities to address critical health challenges. We appreciate the Agency's continued support in advancing animal health, which remains critical to improving livelihood, food security, and agricultural productivity. Kenya takes note of the Agency's efforts in contributing to global food security and welcomes the progress of the Atoms for Food initiative, particularly in regions vulnerable to climate change, land degradation, and nutritional challenges, and look forward to continued collaborations under this important program. Kenya's cooperation with IAEA has been vital in advancing Kenya's development goals in energy diversification, climate adaptation, food security, and healthcare, aligned with our national development priorities, the African Union's Agenda 2063, and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Goals. Key activities included, one, establishing two major cancer treatment centers under the Rays of Hope initiative, significantly improving access to cancer care and strengthening our national capacity for cancer management. Two, strengthening animal health in collaboration with the African Union by an African SASFRI and the Trichomoniasis Eradication Campaign, which advanced the integration of the progressive control pathway into national and regional strategies. Three, establishing the first nuclear power plant by 2034, guided by the IAEA milestones approach as a step towards achieving energy security and mitigating the adverse effects of climate change. And four, capacity building for nuclear engineers and nuclear scientists from the region. Mr. President, Kenya calls for constructive dialogue and cooperation in addressing issues related to noncompliance recognizing that sustained engagement remains key to building mutual confidence and ensuring compliance with international obligations. Kenya remains committed to the highest standards of nuclear safety, security, and safeguards, strengthened through the Nuclear Regulatory Act and the preparation for the upcoming Integrated Regulatory Review Service mission. Through the Kenya Nuclear Regulatory Agency and our national hydrology laboratory, we continue to build regional capacity and foster cooperation in radiation protection and water resource management. In the coming days, Kenya Nuclear Agency Commission and original designated center for entity will be established in line with the agency's best marks. Mr. President, in conclusion, Kenya reaffirms its steadfast commitment to the work and the ideals of the AIEA. We stand ready to deepen cooperation with the Agency and fellow Member States in promoting the peaceful, safe and secure uses of nuclear science and technology for the benefit of humanity and for the sustainable development of present and future generations. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Kenya. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of France.

Mr. President, this year, France has once again co-sponsored resolution on the work of the International Atomic Energy Agency and reaffirms of course its full support for the agency and its activities I would like to make three remarks in this regard first the IAEA plays a crucial role in preserving the international non-proliferation regime and and particularly in the implementation of safeguards under the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons, which is the cornerstone of this regime. At a time when the non-proliferation regime faces major challenges, France reaffirms its unwavering support for the Agency, its Director General, and its teams who carry out their responsibilities with independence and professionalism. on Iran. France calls on Iran to resume full cooperation with the IAEA in line with the agreement and we welcome the IAEA's role of ensuring Iran's compliance with its obligations, particularly those contained in the resolutions recently reinstated by the Security Council. In accordance with those resolutions, Iran must now suspend all of its activities related to enriching and other technical activities with uranium. France is in favor of a diplomatic solution to the Iranian nuclear crisis, which is the only way to ensure over the long term that Iran does not come into possession of nuclear weapons. We call on Iran to come back to the table of negotiations in order to conclude a substantive, lasting, and verifiable agreement regarding its nuclear program. On the issue of North Korea, the ongoing Development by North Korea of its nuclear and ballistic capabilities is, in our view, a serious threat to international peace and security. It is also a blatant violation of international law, including Security Council resolutions. France reiterates its call on North Korea to comply with its international obligations including its obligations under the NPT and to engage in dialogue with a view to a complete, irreversible, and verifiable denuclearization. Now, moving on to my second point, we welcome the IAEA's efforts to disseminate best practices in nuclear safety and security. This contributes to the responsible development of this clean energy source. France condemns in this regard Russia's illegal, firmly condemns Russia's illegal occupation of these Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plants. Russia bears the sole responsibility for the situation and must, as the IA has demanded to put an end to this occupation without delay and to return full control of the facility to Ukrainian authorities. We align ourselves with the joint statement delivered by Ukraine on this matter and reiterate our support for the seven pillars for nuclear safety and security, as well as the five principles set out by the Director General on May 30th, 2023 to the Security Council of the United Nations. The presence of IAEA experts on the ground is a valuable and essential tool that we must collectively encourage and facilitate. Finally, my third point. France supports the Agency's work in promoting the civilian uses of nuclear energy which contributes to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals. My delegation particularly appreciates the IAEA's efforts to shed light on the contribution of nuclear technologies to meeting the challenges of sustainable development and climate change. France is also a supporter of the agency's efforts in the areas of health, food, and agriculture, as well as preserving cultural and natural heritage. This is something where the IAEA possesses recognized expertise. In 2024, France was the sixth largest contributor to the Technical Cooperation Fund and eighth largest contributor to the Fund as an extra budgetary contributor and non-beneficiary. This is a major mechanism that provides access to nuclear technology and know-how. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of France. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Slovenia.

Mr. President, Slovenia aligns itself with the statement delivered by the European Union. In addition, I would like to make the following remarks in our national capacity. We welcome the report of the International Atomic Energy Agency and commend Director General Rafael Grossi and his team for their tireless work and leadership. The IAEA's independent, technical and impartial role remains essential in ensuring that nuclear energy worldwide contributes to peace, security and sustainable development. Slovenia attaches the highest importance to the credibility and integrity of the global nuclear non-proliferation regime, and the IAEA's safeguards system remains its cornerstone. We call for the universalization of comprehensive safeguards agreements and additional protocols, and we continue to support the Agency's efforts to ensure the exclusively peaceful use of nuclear energy. Mr. President, we are deeply concerned about the nuclear safety and security situation in Ukraine, in particular at the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant. Slovenia strongly supports the IAEA's continued presence in Ukraine and endorses the Director General's seven pillars and five principles, which remain crucial as the situation at the plant remains precarious. Slovenia is gravely concerned with the trajectory of DPRK's nuclear program. The international community must create conditions conducive to the DPRK abandoning its illegal WMD and ballistic missile programs. Likewise, we call on Iran to fully cooperate with the IAEA, implement its safeguards obligations, and return to diplomacy to resolve the outstanding issues. Mr. President, as a country operating a nuclear power plant, Krsko Nuclear Power Plant, Slovenia is committed to maintaining the highest standards of nuclear safety, security, and transparency. Our regulatory framework, aligned with Euratom and IAEA standards, ensures the independent oversight of all nuclear activities. Slovenia is committed to a strong nuclear safety and security culture and takes an active part in peer review missions. We are also ensuring the safe, long-term management of radioactive waste, observing international best practices. Mr. President, nuclear energy continues to play a vital role in Slovenia's energy mix. and in our transition to a low-carbon, secure and sustainable energy future. We fully support the IAEA's efforts to promote the peaceful uses of nuclear science and technology in areas such as health, agriculture, water management and environmental protection. Slovenia attaches great importance to international cooperation and capacity building. We appreciate the IAEA's support to Member States through technical cooperation projects and are proud to share our expertise in nuclear safety, nuclear security, regulatory development, and emergency preparedness with regional partners. Last year, we hosted an expert-level workshop in Ljubljana on nuclear safety and security in crisis situations. The discussions reaffirmed the urgent need to strengthen the global nuclear safety framework to address evolving threats. Mr. President, Slovenia commends the Agency's steadfast commitment to advancing gender equality and acknowledges the significant progress made through the Maria Sklodowska-Curie Fellowship Programme. Empowering women to actively participate in nuclear science and policy is crucial for the future of this field. In closing, we reaffirm our unwavering support for the IAEA and the global nuclear non-proliferation regime. We will continue to support the Agency's work in ensuring that nuclear energy is used safely, securely, and exclusively for peaceful purposes. Together, we must preserve the integrity of the international nuclear framework and enable all nations to benefit from the peaceful use of nuclear technology. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Slovenia. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Belarus.

Mr. President, Belarus thanks IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi for his report on the Agency's activities in 2024. We welcome the effective leadership of the organization and highly appreciate the competent work it does in positioning nuclear energy and nuclear technologies as an important component of sustainable development and a safe, reliable, and accessible source of energy. We commend the agency's efforts to expand access to nuclear technologies in energy, healthcare, and agriculture. along with comprehensively strengthening international cooperation in the peaceful uses of nuclear energy. Evidence of these efforts includes the 2024 conferences on nuclear science, on nuclear applications and technical cooperation, as well as the success of the Agency's flagship initiatives. At the same time, The current international context points to a high degree of escalation in this sphere. New security threats pose serious challenges for the IAEA. We express deep concern over the strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities under IAEA safeguards. This contradicts the norms of international law, including the provisions of the 1968 Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons and the Geneva Conventions. Such actions lead to serious humanitarian consequences. They endanger the safety of civilians as well as the environment, and they also carry the risk of catastrophe for the entire nonproliferation regime. We once again call on the international community to give due attention to the situation. Wisdom and foresight must prevail over emotions and prejudice. We urge the IAEA to take a thoughtful and principled approach to situations that involve a threat to nuclear safety. Equally importantly, in a period of major international turbulence, the IAEA as a central international platform must maintain its depoliticized nature and act strictly in accordance with its mandate. Only strengthened cooperation and impartial work by the Agency can make the sustainable development of peaceful nuclear energy possible. In terms of bilateral cooperation between Belarus and the IAEA, we would like to note the following. For five years now, Belarus has been operating its first nuclear power plant. The construction of the Belarusian NPP has enabled our country to ensure energy security and technological sovereignty. The commissioning of the plant has allowed to meet the growing demand for electricity. The nuclear power plant covers two-fifths of national electricity needs. It is equally important that thanks to the operation of the Belarusian nuclear power plant, the country has reduced its annual greenhouse gas emissions by more than 7 million tons. From the very beginning of implementing its national nuclear energy program, Belarus has taken significant steps towards establishing a system of nuclear and radiation safety, as well as its key elements, creating the necessary legal framework, as well as building and operating a protection and response system. The Republic of Belarus is fully implementing its international obligations to ensure the required level of physical protection of nuclear material and facilities at the Belarusian nuclear power plant. During last year's visit to the plant, IAEA Director General, as well as other senior leaders of the agency, were able to witness the safe and effective functioning of this facility firsthand. We highly appreciate this visit as well as the substantive discussion of the full range of cooperation issues that took place during it. The year 2026 will once again recall the tragic legacy of the Chernobyl disaster. In this context, the signing of a document on practical cooperation between the Agency and the Polesia Radioecological Reserve ahead of the 40th anniversary of the tragedy is highly meaningful for us. Belarus reaffirms its readiness for transparent and responsible cooperation. We are prepared to share our experience in developing nuclear energy infrastructure. We remain open to constructive, professional, expert dialogue on nuclear safety with all interested parties. Thank you for your attention.
I thank the distinguished representative of Belarus. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of the Maldives.

Thank you, Mr. President. The Maldives thanks the Director-General and the Secretariat for presenting the report, which provides a comprehensive account of the Agency's activities and priorities over the past year. The Maldives recognizes the value that that nuclear science brings to public welfare when governed with rigor and transparency. The IAEA ensures that benefit and responsibility advance together. I thank the distinguished representative of Maldives. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Libya.

I thank the distinguished representative of Libya. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Portugal.

We greatly value the work of the agency in Ukraine, namely with regard to the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant. We're very proud to have been elected last September to the agency's Board of Governors. Mr. President, concluding, even as we approach next year's NPT Review Conference, it is clear that the nuclear disarmament architecture is eroding. Mr. President, I commend the Director General, Rafael Maria Mugrabi, for presenting the Agency's annual report and for his visionary leadership throughout his two terms. I thank the distinguished representative of Algeria. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of the Russian Federation.

Mr. President, the Russian Federation attaches great importance to the work of the International Atomic Energy Agency, which is an important instrument of international cooperation in the peaceful uses of atomic energy, as well as a unique mechanism for monitoring states' compliance with their nuclear nonproliferation obligations. We are convinced that the footnote included in the draft, which merely refers to a lengthy compendium of resolutions and decisions of the General Conference, cannot be considered an adequate substitute for a factual mention of those resolutions which were put to a vote. We see this as an attempt to conceal the fact that these politically motivated initiatives do not enjoy universal support and create division within the agency. We condemn and reject the provisions of any agency documents that contradict objective reality and deny the voluntary reunification of Crimea, Sevastopol, the Donetsk and Luhansk People's Republics and the Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions with Russia, as well as Russia's ownership of nuclear facilities and sites outside facilities where nuclear material is used in these regions of our country. And this, despite the fact that the only party creating threats to the nuclear safety and security in the current conflict is Ukraine. This is clearly illustrated by the repeated attacks carried out by Kyiv against the ZNPP over the past three years. I will not go into the details of these reckless actions. as our country regularly informs the IAEA Secretariat, the UN Security Council, and the international community as a whole about the real situation at the nuclear power plant. An IAEA mission is present at the ZNPP, and its experts have had the opportunity to see firsthand who is actually creating threats to the nuclear power plants. We expect that they will be able to inform the international community about this and directly name the source of the attacks, the armed forces of Ukraine. Ukraine, for its part, is doing everything possible to demonstrate its disregard both for the agency's efforts, including by promoting politicized initiatives in the UN General Assembly that undermine the IAEA's work, as well as disregard for basic common sense. we stress that the ZNPP is a Russian facility. Our country independently determines the parameters for the functioning of the plant's relevant safety systems, as we bear responsibility for ensuring nuclear safety and security on our territory. We will continue to do everything necessary in this regard in accordance with our national legislation and international obligations. We will also keep the international community informed about the real situation at the ZNPP. Mr. President, We also note the fundamentally erroneous, biased, and destructive nature of the agency's resolution entitled Implementation of the NPT Safeguards Agreement between the Agency and the DPRK. The reason is simple. The data underpinning this document, which was drawn from the relevant agency report, raised legitimate questions and have not been verified through an inspection since IAEA inspectors have not visited the nuclear facilities of that state for more than 15 years. It is striking in this context that a number of countries continue to talk about a certain goal of the DPRK's denuclearization. Russia is also being absurdly reproached for rejecting this objective and legitimately developing bilateral relations with our close neighbor and longstanding partner. It is absolutely clear that responsibility for the escalation of tensions on the Korean Peninsula lies with Western states. Instead of seeking political and diplomatic solutions, the United States and their regional allies, primarily the Republic of Korea and Japan, have been conducting annual large-scale military exercises targeting the DPRK for half a century now. This irresponsible, confrontational, and provocative policy poses a real threat to regional security and does nothing to help reduce tensions on the Korean Peninsula. Mr. President, in conclusion, we would like to draw attention to the fact that any politically motivated statements by the President of the General Assembly are absolutely unacceptable. In accordance with the PGA Code of Ethics enshrined in Resolution 70/305 and reaffirmed in Resolution 79/327, I remind you that the President of the General Assembly in their work must maintain an impartial and unbiased position. We call on the PGA to refrain in the future from any unfounded insinuations regarding the Ukrainian issue, as well as baseless accusations against UN member states, the invalidity of which we have regularly demonstrated in relevant forms. Thank you for your attention.
I thank the distinguished representative of the Russian Federation. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Hungary.

Mr. President, Hungary welcomes the adoption of the report of the IAEA in advance and wishes to emphasize the Agency's indispensable contribution to promoting its mandate of atoms for peace and development. We express our appreciation to Director General Rafael Grossi for his leadership and for this comprehensive report. We are also grateful to Australia for their able chairmanship in the IAEA Board of Governors. In a time marked by increasing global challenges, Hungary attaches particular importance to the IAEA's independent and impartial work, which continues to serve as a cornerstone of transparency and cooperation in the nuclear field. Hungary aligns itself with the main aspects of the EU statement regarding the EU support for the IAEA Comprehensive Safeguard Agreement and the Additional Protocol, the UN Security Council Resolution 2231, and the objectives and principles of the NPT. In relation to Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine, we believe that we are facing new geopolitical circumstances and the conflict has entered a new phase to which the international community needs to adapt its policymaking. Therefore, in this regard, Hungary has more reservations compared to other EU member states. Hungary reaffirms its enduring commitment to the global non-proliferation architecture. We remain steadfast in supporting the IAEA's central role in preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons while promoting and facilitating peaceful uses of nuclear energy under appropriate safeguards. Hungary considers the Comprehensive Safeguards Agreement together with the additional protocols as the standard for verification. The IAEA safeguards system is a crucial measure to maintain international security and confidence. As highlighted in the report, the Agency also plays an important role in achieving the Sustainable Development Goals by assisting Member States in using nuclear technology for health, food security, water management and environmental protection. We emphasize the indivisibility of its three pillars, nonproliferation, disarmament, and the peaceful use of nuclear energy. We support all diplomatic efforts aimed at each achieving the complete, verifiable, and irreversible dismantlement of the DPRK's nuclear program. We call upon the DPRK to return to the MPT and to cooperate fully with the IAEA. In conclusion, let me once again reiterate that Hungary strongly supports the IAEA's work in reinforcing international security, maintaining the integrity of non-proliferation regime, and facilitating responsible international cooperation on peaceful nuclear applications. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Hungary. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of South Africa.

Mr. President, South Africa welcomes the 2024 annual report of the International Atomic Energy Agency and commends the agency for its continued dedication to advancing the peaceful uses of nuclear science and technology in these challenging geopolitical times. In this regard, South Africa underscores the importance of strengthening the IAEA safeguard system within the framework of the NPT to ensure trust, ensure compliance, and reinforce the integrity of the non-proliferation regime. Mr. President, in 2024, cooperation between South Africa and the IAEA depend across key areas. The signing of our fifth country programme framework, 2024-2029, provides a strong foundation for collaboration in nuclear safety, health, food and agriculture, water management and industrial innovation. We are also proud that the nuclear medicine research infrastructure was designated as an IAEA collaborating center under the Rays of Hope Cancer Care for All initiative. alongside our ongoing cooperation with eThemba Labs to strengthen regional capacity in accelerator-based science and technology. South Africa remains fully committed to the Agency's mandate and to ensuring that nuclear technology continues to advance peace, prosperity, and the attainment of the goals of the UN 2030 Agenda and Africa's Agenda 2063. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of South Africa. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of the Republic of Korea.

Chair, we extend our appreciation to Director General of the IAEA, Rafael Grossi, for presenting the 2024 Annual Report, and to the distinguished representative of Australia for introducing draft resolution A/80/L.7, which we happily co-sponsored. Our decision to host an international ministerial conference on nuclear power in 2026 underscores our steadfast commitment to the IAEA's mandate to promote atoms for peace and development. We continue to fully support the IAEA's efforts to universalize the comprehensive safeguard agreements and additional protocol, and the revised small quantities protocol. We urge all those that have not yet done so to conclude and bring these key instruments into force without delay. My delegation welcomes the resolution implementation of the NPT safeguards agreements between the Agency and the DPRK. which was adopted by an overwhelming majority at the 69th IAEA General Conference. Once again, the resolution clearly states that the DPRK cannot have the status of a nuclear weapons state in accordance with the NPT, and that all member states should fully, comprehensively, and immediately implement relevant UN Security Council resolutions. We once again urge the DPRK to fully comply with all its international obligations, cease all provocations and its illegal nuclear and ballistic missile programs, take concrete steps toward complete denuclearization, and return to dialogue at all stages. The Republic of Korea also takes note of the IAEA General Conference resolution on nuclear safety, security and safeguards in Ukraine, adopted for the third time since the onset of the war against Ukraine. Over the past three years, the precarious nuclear safety and security situation in Ukraine has shown no sign of improvement. We reiterate our full support for the continued efforts of the IAEA Director General and his team to closely monitor and report on the situation, including through the continued on site presence of the IAEA support and assistant mission to Japan. Regarding the disposal of contaminated water stored at the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station, We appreciate the agency's dedicated efforts over the past two years. We expect the IAEA to continue its on-site monitoring and independent analysis to ensure that the discharge remains fully consistent with international safety standards. The Republic of Korea reaffirms its commitment to actively participating in the IAEA monitoring and corroboration activities. Chair. The Republic of Korea has been an active contributor to expanding the benefits of peaceful uses of nuclear energy through its support for various IAEA technical cooperation programs, such as Rays of Hope, JODIAP, New Tech Plastics, Renewal, Atoms for Food, and the Peaceful Use Initiative. We reaffirm our support for the IAS platform on small modular reactors and their applications, as well as the nuclear harmonization and standardization initiative, both of which play a crucial role in the development of advanced reactors under appropriate regular regulatory frameworks. We also welcome the agency's effort to apply artificial intelligence across the nuclear technology life cycle. We will take an active part in the discourse on its safe and effective application at the upcoming International Symposium on AI and Nuclear Energy in December 2025. Chair, we wish to reiterate the importance of enhancing the representation and participation of Member States in the IAEA Board of Governors. It remains a matter of concern that, even after 26 years, The amendment to Article 6 of the IAEA Statute has yet to enter into force. The amendment aims to align the composition of the Board with the Agency's growing membership and evolving nuclear landscape, thereby ensuring greater equity and inclusiveness in its governance. We encourage all Member States that have not yet done so to take the necessary step toward ratification. Finally, taking this opportunity, we commend the Agency for achieving gender parity among its staff, with women now accounting for more than 50% of the professional and higher categories. At the same time, we encourage the Secretariat to further strengthen its efforts to improve geographical representation. with particular attention to regions, including the Far East, which remains underrepresented. With these remarks, we affirm our strong support for the work of the Agency, as well as the draft resolution A/80/L.7, report of the International Atomic Energy Agency. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of the Republic of Korea. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of the Islamic Republic of Iran.

In the name of God, the compassionate and merciful, Mr. President, I thank the Director General for his report. However, such reports must always remain professional, factual, and free from political influence. The credibility of the agency depends entirely on its impartiality. Nuclear energy is indispensable for development and energy security, particularly for developing countries. The transfer of nuclear science and technology granted under Article IV of the NPT and the IAEA Statute is an inalienable right, not a privilege. Safeguard must facilitate, not obstruct, the peaceful use of nuclear energy. Many attempts to exploit proliferation concerns to deny developing countries their legitimate rights constitute a serious violation of the NPT's letter and spirit. It is alarming that while Certain states systematically restrict developing nations' access to peaceful nuclear technology. They simultaneously arm and assist the Israeli regime, a regime outside the NPT, with a clandestine arsenal of weapons of mass destruction. Such double standards, combined with unlawful, unilateral coercive measures, gravely undermine the credibility of the non-proliferation regime and the Agency's technical cooperation mandate, Mr. President. In June 2025, the world witnessed an atrocious act of aggression. The Israeli regime, only hours after a politically motivated resolution in the IAEA Board of Governors, launched massive military strike against Iran's safeguard nuclear facilities. Under full agency monitoring, this criminal attack targeted Iranian scientists and their families, killing and injuring thousands and inflicting immense material damage. On 22 June, the United States, a permanent member of the Security Council and depository of the NPT, joined this aggression, directly targeting IAEA-monitored facilities. This act flagrantly violated international law, the UN Charter, IAEA Statute and Security Council Resolution 487, which explicitly prohibits attack on safeguard nuclear installations. This was not merely an attack on one member state. It was an assault on the authority of the United Nations, the credibility of the agency and integrity of the safeguard system itself. While relevant General Conference resolutions, in particular, resolution 444 and resolution 533, explicitly affirm that any armed attack on or threat against nuclear facilities devoted to peaceful purposes constitute a violation of the principles of the UN Charter, international law, and the Statute of the Agency. And while the Director General has repeatedly emphasized that nuclear facilities must never be attacked under any circumstances due to the grave risk such actions pose to people, the environment, and to nuclear safety, security, and safeguards, as well as regional and international peace and security, it is deeply regrettable that the illegal attacks against Iran peaceful nuclear facilities were neither condemned by the Agency, nor by the Security Council, nor indeed by the Director General himself. Regrettably, both the President of the General Assembly and the Director General of the IAEA, in their statement under this agenda item, have once again failed to condemn these illegal attacks. Mr. President, Iran has been a responsible party to the NPT since 1970. Yet, the E3 and the United States, echoing Israeli regime fabrications, continue to misrepresent Iran's peaceful nuclear activities, while the Israeli regime, the region's sole possessor of nuclear weapons and main obstacle to a nuclear-weapon-free Middle East, acts with complete impunity. Despite sabotage, assassination, and unlawful sanctions, and no direct attacks on our safeguard facilities, Iran has never violated the GCPOA, the NPT, or its safeguard obligations, and has remained committed to diplomacy. The recent report of the Director General confirmed that the suspension of inspections was a direct consequence of this armed attack. responsibility lies entirely with the aggressor, not with the victim. No safeguards provision currently address how to maintain engagement under condition of armed aggression and continuing threats. A new framework is therefore required to ensure that the safety of nuclear personnel and facilities under such extraordinary circumstances. In a constructive spirit, Iran and the Agency signed a Memorandum of Understanding in Cairo on 9 September 2025, aimed at addressing these challenges. Unfortunately, this positive development was immediately undermined by the hostile action of the United States and E3, who continue to block every diplomatic initiative, including the balanced proposal by China and Russia in the Security Council. The E3's invocation of the so-called snapback mechanism, an illegal reckless act aimed at destroying the last bridge to diplomacy, is null and void. Having themselves violated the GCP and resolution 2231, they have no legal standing to invoke its provisions. Resolution 2231 expires permanently on 18th October, 2025. and all related restrictions are terminated. Any attempt to revive or reinforce them is an illegal abuse of process and must be rejected by this Assembly and by the Secretary-General. Mr. President, Iran will never yield to threats or coercion. We respond only to respect, legality, and equality. Military aggression and economic terrorism will not compel Iran to abandon its legitimate rights. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of the Islamic Republic of Iran. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Cuba.

Mr. President, we're grateful for the presentation of the annual report of the International Atomic Energy Agency and the draft resolution A/80/L/7. We reiterate Cuba's support for this important agency and its contribution to the peaceful use of nuclear energy. In this context, we reiterate our strongest condemnation of Israeli and United States air strikes on nuclear installations in the Islamic Republic of Iran last June. President, We wish to thank the Agency for the efforts in addressing mosquito-borne diseases such as Zika, dengue and chikungunya. We also wish to flag the support of the Cooperation Department as an essential mechanism to give countries of the global south access to nuclear technologies with a social impact. Together, we have developed in the areas of nuclear medicine, particularly looking at cancer control, food security, environmental protection. We reaffirm Cuba's commitment to the peaceful use of nuclear energy and the great importance that we attach to nuclear and radiological safety. President, despite the noteworthy cooperation between Cuba and the IAEA, we cannot but mention the problems that this agency commonly faces in implementing its projects with our country due to the restrictions imposed by the economic, commercial, and financial blockade of the US against Cuba. The prohibition on countries from the US, or even those in third countries that have US shareholders, from selling equipment to Cuba continues to drive up the cost of procurement for equipment for our country, hindering capacity building, delaying the rollout of national projects under the auspices of the IAEA, and leaving us out of opportunities for projects in our region. We reject unilateral coercive measures that contravene Article IV of the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons. They obstruct international cooperation and block access to material, equipment and technologies for peaceful nuclear activities by developing countries that are subjected to this type of measure. President, the IAEA provides the framework for the adoption of international standards on nuclear safety that should be the outcome of transparent and inclusive multilateral negotiations involving all states. Contrary to the benefits for humanity of peaceful nuclear energy, the mere existence of nuclear weapons continues to threaten the survival of the human race. We continue to believe that the only safeguard against the use or the threat of use of nuclear weapons is their full elimination in a verifiable, transparent, and irreversible manner. Accordingly, we advocate for the universalization of the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons without delay. The goal of nuclear disarmament cannot continue to be indefinitely postponed. Thank you very much.
I thank the distinguished representative of Cuba. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative for Fiji.

Mr. President, Fiji wishes to join the chorus of gratitude extended in this hall to the Director General, Mr. Rafael Grossi, for the IAEA report. Through you, Mr. President, we also like to thank IAEA staff for their enduring support and partnership with small island developing states like Fiji, including their resilience in working in some of the dangerous and complex zones of our time in ensuring peace and security. We also convey our gratitude to Australia as Chair of the IAEA Board of Governors for introducing the resolution in relation to IAEA's annual report, which Fiji gladly cosponsors. Mr. President, At the 54th Pacific Island Forum in the Solomon Islands in September this year, Pacific leaders endorsed the Ocean of Peace Declaration, reaffirming the Pacific region's commitment to a nuclear-free region and peace as we commemorate this year's 40th anniversary of the Treaty of Rarotonga. Fiji supports the critical role of the IAEA in ensuring the implementation of appropriate safeguards for the non-proliferation of nuclear weapons. In relation to the Advanced Liquid Processing System water discharge, Fiji aligns with the Pacific Leaders Communique adopted this year. in welcoming the ongoing efforts by the Pacific community to develop a guidance and assessment scientific data on all nuclear related discharge and community contamination issues. This also includes a region's MOU on ALPS with the IAEA. Additionally, my Prime Minister, the Honorable Sita Bin Ramuka, had a fruitful meeting in Japan yesterday. her excellency the Prime Minister Takechi in relation to this matter. We signed our IAEA country program framework from 2022 to 27 in line with IAEA's nuclear science and technology program. Our technical cooperation program will focus on strengthening agricultural resilience and food security via mutation breeding, addressing climate change impacts, and through isotope hydrology for water resources, and also establishing radiotherapy facilities for health and managing the legacy of radioactive sources. As a small island developing state in a region vulnerable to climate change, this support is not just technical, it's existential. Additionally, as a member state since 2012, IAEA's technical assistance is targeted towards Fiji's achievement of its national development goals, with a particular focus on food and security, health, water and environment protection. Last year, Fiji accepted the modified small quantity protocol and has since been providing declarations to each additional protocol, the latest of which was submitted in September this year in Vienna. Additionally, in 2024, with the support of IAEA experts, Fiji successfully extracted and exported disused radioactive sources to the USA for cancer treatment purposes. Fiji values the importance of working with IAEA for security and safety purposes. This includes hosting technical missions to Fiji, compiling its source inventory and working with border agencies, encouraging national regulators to monitor operations continuously, and holding quarterly national interagency with IAEA counterparts for greater transparency. Mr. President, as the current chair of the Regional Co-operative Agreement of the IAEA, we have hosted national representatives from Asia and the Pacific in Fiji in May this year. We also chaired the Regional Co-operative Agency for the IAEA in the margins of the General Conference meeting in Vienna last month in preparation for the 69th IAEA General Conference. In closing, Fiji looks forward to deepening its partnership with the IAEA, recognising that science and solidarity together can shape a safer, healthier, and more prosperous future for all. I thank you.

We continue to fully support the establishment of a zone free of nuclear and all other weapons of mass destruction and their delivery systems in the Middle East, as agreed at the 1995 NPT Review Conference. The EU strongly supports the strengthening of the IAEA safeguards system. For decades, Euratom has guaranteed nuclear materials controls in Europe and has served as a reliable partner to the IAEA in nuclear safeguards, remaining a key contributor to global nonproliferation efforts. Comprehensive safeguards agreements, together with additional protocols, represent the current verification standard under Article III of the NPT. and we call for their universalization without delay. The IAEA safeguards system is a fundamental component of the nuclear non-proliferation regime and plays an indispensable role in the implementation of the NPT. We underline the primary responsibility of the UN Security Council in cases of non-compliance and encourage diplomatic efforts to find peaceful solutions to proliferation crises which represent a grave threat to international and regional peace and security. Mr. President, The EU and its Member States attach utmost importance to nuclear safety and its continuous improvement and calls on all States to make use of the IAEA review services. EURATOM has built up an advanced, legally binding and enforceable nuclear safety legal framework, which is applicable in all EURATOM Member States. Other countries also benefit from our assistance with a budget of 300 million euros. We encourage all UN Member States to promote a strong nuclear safety culture. We look forward to the next review meeting of the Convention on Nuclear Safety in April 2026. We encourage all UN Member States to join the International Nuclear Safety and Security Conventions, as well as the Code of Conduct on Radioactive Resources sources. We appreciate the agency's continued commitment to maintaining fully applicable and up-to-date safety standards and security guidance. Also, for new technology concepts such as small modular reactors, it is particularly important to ensure the highest level of nuclear safety and security. in accordance with the IAEA safety standards and security guidance. We also note the fast development of artificial intelligence and its applications worldwide. We look forward to the IAEA's Tech Doc on safety and security implications of the use of artificial intelligence in nuclear installations and the upcoming International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Nuclear Energy. The EU and its Member States support the IAEA's activities in the peaceful uses of nuclear science and technology to implement the 2030 Agenda on Sustainable Development and the Paris Climate Agreements.
